name: Luke Farritor
milestone_by_age_26: In October 2023, at age ~21, won the Vesuvius Challenge First Letters Prize ($40,000) as the first person to recover a complete word (ΠΟΡΦΥΡΑϹ, 'purple') from an unopened Herculaneum scroll using machine learning on CT scans.
early_history_summary: Lincoln, Nebraska native and son of UNL robotics professor Shane Farritor; studied computer science at the Raikes School at University of Nebraska–Lincoln and interned at SpaceX. While still an undergrad, he trained ML models on flattened Herculaneum papyrus volumes, first finding letters and then the full word that won the First Letters Prize, then co-won the $700,000 Grand Prize in February 2024.
secondary_engine: Structural wave (open AI challenges + CT virtual unwrapping)
family_context_summary: Son of Shane Farritor, a University of Nebraska–Lincoln engineering professor and robotics researcher from Ravenna, Nebraska; grew up in the Lincoln academic/tech environment.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father is a mechanical engineering / robotics professor at UNL; domain-adjacent technical household and university lab ecosystem rather than a direct computer-vision apprenticeship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: academic parent household, SpaceX internship, open competition prize path, ML crackle detection
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, Vesuvius Challenge official prize pages, TIME, and UNL/Nebraska Today independently document Farritor as ~21 in Oct 2023 when he won First Letters and as grand-prize co-winner in Feb 2024. Birth year reported as 2001/2002; age-at-milestone ~21 is consistent across sources. Father Shane Farritor is a named UNL professor. Later Thiel Fellowship (2024) and DOGE role roles followed the scroll work.
starting_point: Born ~2001/2002 in Nebraska to a university robotics professor; raised in Lincoln with early access to engineering culture and later the UNL Raikes School CS program.
current_position: Software engineer known for Vesuvius Challenge wins; Thiel Fellow; worked on Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) / federal tech roles in 2025.

trajectory.event: As a SpaceX intern and UNL CS student, won the Vesuvius Challenge First Letters Prize for recovering the first full word from a Herculaneum scroll via ML.
Co-won the $700,000 Vesuvius Challenge Grand Prize with Youssef Nader and Julian Schilliger; later named a Thiel Fellow and left UNL.
Joined DOGE / related federal tech efforts with high-level system access at GSA and other agencies; converted to full-time GS-15 federal employee.

name: Myra B. Cohen
milestone_by_age_26: No specific dated material milestone by age 26 found; career breakout is academic (MS Vermont 1999; PhD Auckland 2004 on combinatorial software interaction testing; later professorships at Nebraska and Iowa State).
family_context_summary: Originally from New York City; not otherwise documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Iowa State faculty pages document an agriculture/life-sciences start at Cornell, hospital data-analyst path into CS, MS (1999), PhD (2004). Without a birth year and with major recognition (ACM Distinguished Member 2017, endowed chairs) arriving well into a faculty career, no age-≤26 material milestone can be verified.

name: Christopher Olah
milestone_by_age_26: In 2012, at age 19, awarded a $100,000 Thiel Fellowship for independent technical work after dropping out of University of Toronto; by 2015 (~age 22) he was an intern/research scientist track at Google Brain working on neural network visualization.
early_history_summary: Canadian; grew up in the Toronto tech/hacker scene (hacklab.to), experimented with 3D printing and open-source fabrication as a teenager, briefly attended University of Toronto for math then left around age 18. The 2012 Thiel Fellowship funded self-directed work that led into machine learning research and, within a few years, Google Brain.
family_context_summary: Mother Frances Zomer publicly discussed his upbringing (including bullying) in a CNBC Thiel Fellows piece; detailed family financial/domain background otherwise limited in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a technical or AI-domain family apprenticeship in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Thiel Fellowship, hackerspace youth, blog/Distill communication, Google Brain entry
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, Forbes, CNBC, and 80,000 Hours agree he was ~19 for the 2012 Thiel Fellowship (born 1992 or 1993; coded 1993). Google Brain start ~2015, Distill co-founding 2017/2018, OpenAI interpretability lead 2018, Anthropic co-founding 2021 are well documented. Family advantage scores kept low/zero where sources do not support them.
starting_point: Born in Canada ~1992/1993; Toronto youth involved in hackerspaces and DIY tech; left University of Toronto without a degree after about a year.
current_position: Co-founder of Anthropic and leading mechanistic interpretability researcher; TIME100 AI (2024); Forbes has reported billionaire status from Anthropic equity.

trajectory.event: Named a Thiel Fellow ($100k) at age 19 after leaving University of Toronto; pursued independent technical work (initially including 3D printing).
Joined Google Brain as an intern and advanced into neural network visualization / interpretability research (including DeepDream-era work).
Left Google Brain to lead OpenAI’s interpretability (Clarity) team; Distill journal work elevated public ML communication.
Co-founded Anthropic after leaving OpenAI; continued as technical staff focused on mechanistic interpretability and AI safety.
Named to TIME100 AI for pioneering mechanistic interpretability across Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic.

name: Jean Sammet
milestone_by_age_26: No material field-defining milestone by age 26; began professional programming on SPEEDAC in January 1955 at age 26 as entry-level systems work. COBOL design contribution was 1959 (age 31); FORMAC at IBM was 1962 (age 34).
family_context_summary: Born in New York City to Harry and Ruth Sammet, both lawyers; attended public schools and Mount Holyoke (BA math 1948) then Illinois (MA 1949).
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were lawyers; no documented computer or engineering domain transfer (computers barely existed in her childhood).
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and IEEE Annals / NYT obituary timeline: BA 1948, MA 1949, Sperry mathematician from 1953, first programming assignment Jan 1955 (age 26), COBOL 1959, FORMAC 1962, ACM president 1974–76. Defining achievements land after 26.

name: Thomas E. Anderson
milestone_by_age_26: No material research or systems milestone by age 26 found; Harvard BA (philosophy) 1983 at age 21–22, then UW CS MS 1989 and PhD 1991 (age ~30) before Berkeley faculty appointment. Major awards (Weiser, NAE, etc.) came decades later.
family_context_summary: Born August 28, 1961 in Orlando, Florida; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and UW faculty bio: b. 1961, Harvard AB 1983, UW PhD 1991 under Lazowska/Levy, Berkeley then UW faculty. Field leadership (distributed systems, networking, OS textbook) and NAE membership are mid/late-career.

name: Conal Elliott
milestone_by_age_26: No verified material milestone by age 26; BA math UCSB CCS 1982, PhD CMU 1990 (higher-order unification), then Sun Labs / Microsoft Research work that produced Functional Reactive Programming in the mid-1990s—well after any plausible age-26 window.
evidence_summary: Personal site and conference bios list BA 1982, PhD 1990 (CMU under Frank Pfenning), MSR ~1994–2002 where FRP/ActiveVRML work crystallized. Exact birth year not found; defining FRP contribution is mid-career relative to education timeline.

name: Alan Kay
milestone_by_age_26: No material career-defining milestone by age 26; BS Colorado 1966 at age 26, MS Utah 1968 (FLEX language) at 28, PhD 1969 at 29, joined Xerox PARC in 1970 at 30 where Smalltalk, Dynabook, and modern GUI work made his lasting impact.
family_context_summary: Born Springfield, Massachusetts; family relocated with father's physiology career; grandson of author/illustrator Clifton Johnson; early voracious reader.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father worked in physiology; not a computer-science apprenticeship (field did not yet exist as such).
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and ACM Turing Award materials: b. May 17, 1940; Air Force programmer after draft; BS 1966; Utah MS/PhD late 1960s; PARC from 1970. Legendary OOP/GUI achievements and 2003 Turing Award are post-26.

name: Trip Adler
milestone_by_age_26: In March 2007, at age ~22–23, co-founded and launched Scribd out of a San Francisco apartment after Y Combinator (summer 2006), building one of the early successful document-sharing and later ebook subscription platforms.
early_history_summary: Grew up in Palo Alto, attended Gunn High School, graduated Harvard biophysics 2006. After several false-start startup ideas, co-founded Scribd with classmate Jared Friedman (and Tikhon Bernstam), entered Y Combinator, and shipped the product in 2007.
family_context_summary: Raised in Palo Alto; father John R. Adler is a Stanford neurosurgeon and entrepreneur whose difficulty publishing an academic paper helped inspire Scribd.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father is a prominent Stanford neurosurgeon/entrepreneur; not a software product apprenticeship, but high-status professional family and direct story spark for document publishing.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Palo Alto, Harvard, Y Combinator, cofounder Jared Friedman, physician-entrepreneur father
evidence_summary: Bizjournals (born Palo Alto 1984), Wikipedia, Harvard SEAS profile, LA Times, and YC alumni coverage align: Harvard ’06, YC 2006, Scribd launch March 2007 at age ~22–23. Later CEO until 2023; founded Created by Humans in 2024.
starting_point: Born 1984 in Palo Alto to a Stanford neurosurgeon father; Gunn High School then Harvard biophysics; Bay Area tech geography from birth.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Created by Humans (AI training-rights marketplace for authors); previously co-founder and CEO of Scribd (2007–2023).

trajectory.event: Graduated Harvard; entered Y Combinator summer batch with Jared Friedman to build what became Scribd.
Launched Scribd from San Francisco as co-founder/CEO, creating a major document-sharing platform.
Scribd expanded into a paid ebook subscription service competing as a 'Netflix for books'.
Stepped down as Scribd CEO after ~16 years leading the company.
Co-founded Created by Humans to license authors’ works for AI training.

name: Karen Casella
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; WPI mechanical engineering BS 1983, early career at Maxtor, then software engineer/architect at Sun Microsystems from 1993—leadership roles at eBay, SHOP.COM, and Netflix came well into mid-career.
family_context_summary: Grew up on the South Shore of Massachusetts; family engineering interest noted in WPI profile but not detailed.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in detail in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and WPI alumni profile: BS ME 1983, Maxtor, Sun from 1993, later eBay/SHOP.COM VP roles and Netflix edge/playback engineering leadership. Exact birth year missing; no dated ≤26 breakout identified.

name: Michael Brooks
milestone_by_age_26: Could not verify age at PhoneGap/Apache Cordova contributions; listed among original Cordova authors and long-time PhoneGap/Adobe/Nitobi engineer, but no reliable birth year or dated ≤26 milestone found (batch Wikipedia URL is ambiguous).
evidence_summary: Apache Cordova Wikipedia lists Michael Brooks among original authors; personal site/LinkedIn (michaelbrooks.ca, University of Regina, later Slack open-source) confirm PhoneGap/Cordova CLI work. Without birth year, age-≤26 eligibility cannot be established.

name: Jim Highsmith
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; defining work is Adaptive Software Development (1999 book, age ~54) and co-signing the Agile Manifesto (2001, age ~56) after decades as an IT manager/consultant.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia: born 1945; Adaptive Software Development (1999), Jolt Award (2000), Agile Manifesto signatory (2001), Stevens Award (2005). Long IT career before public methodology fame; nothing dated ≤26.

name: Brittney Exline
milestone_by_age_26: In May 2011, at age 19, graduated cum laude from the University of Pennsylvania with a BSE in computer science—reported as Penn’s youngest engineer graduate and the nation’s youngest African-American engineer—after entering an Ivy League program at 15.
early_history_summary: Born February 14, 1992 in Colorado Springs; taught herself to read at age 2, skipped three grades, completed an IB high-school program, and enrolled at Penn on full scholarship in 2007 at 15. Earned a CS engineering degree at 19 and entered industry as a software engineer (Chitika).
family_context_summary: Daughter of Chyrese and Christopher Exline; Colorado Springs upbringing. Detailed socioeconomic background not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a software-engineering family apprenticeship in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early literacy, grade acceleration, Ivy League at 15, Penn CS at 19
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, Ebony, The Root, and NewsOne concur on birth date 1992-02-14, Ivy admission at 15 (2007), and Penn CS graduation cum laude at 19 (2011) with national 'youngest African-American engineer' coverage. Later industry path less documented; scores conservative outside prodigy/institution signals.
starting_point: Born 1992 in Colorado Springs to Chyrese and Christopher Exline; extreme early academic acceleration (read at 2; skipped grades).
current_position: Software engineer; early career included Chitika after Penn; later public profile primarily historical as youngest African-American engineer graduate.

trajectory.event: Enrolled at the University of Pennsylvania on full scholarship at age 15, reported as the youngest African-American female accepted to an Ivy League school.
Graduated cum laude with a BSE in computer science from Penn—national coverage as youngest African-American engineer and youngest Penn engineer.
Began professional software engineering work (reported role at online advertising firm Chitika) after graduation.
